What is procured: NHPC Limited is procuring 1200 MW of 'Firm & Dispatchable' renewable power from ISTS-connected RE power projects coupled with energy storage systems, on an anywhere-in-India basis under tariff based competitive bidding (Tranche-II, Open Category), with selection through an e-reverse auction. [1][2][3][4][5][6][7] Each bidder may offer a minimum of 50 MW and a maximum of 600 MW. [8][9][10][11] Storage is mandatory: the developer must combine RE generation with ESS to supply the contracted capacity at a minimum 90% availability during peak hours and at a declared annual CUF of not less than 40%. [12][13][14][15][16][17]

Buyer and offtaker: NHPC Limited issues the RfS and signs the Power Purchase Agreement with the selected bidders. [18][19][20] NHPC acts as Intermediary Procurer and trading licensee under the PPA, selling the power back-to-back under Power Sale Agreements to the Buying Entities (Discoms), who are the end procurers. [21][22] The Buying Entities will be named later. [23]

Location: Projects may be set up anywhere in India, connected to the ISTS, on land identified and arranged by the developer, who must show possession of 100% of the land in its name for the full PPA term on or before the Scheduled Commencement of Supply Date. [24][25][26][27][28] The delivery point is the point at 220 kV or above at the CTU substation where the power from the project is injected into the ISTS; metering is on the low voltage side of the CTU/STU substation or, for RE parks, at the pooling station. [29][30][31] The developer builds and pays for the dedicated transmission line up to the Interconnection Point with no reimbursement, and the proposed location may be changed only up to Financial Closure. [32][33][34][35][36]

Timeline: The RfS was issued on 15 March 2024, queries were due by 26 March 2024, the pre-bid meeting was on 28 March 2024, bids were due by 12 April 2024 and technical bids were to be opened on 17 April 2024. [37][38][39][40][41][42][43] Bids are valid for 180 days; the e-reverse auction and price bid opening dates are not printed and are to be intimated separately by NHPC. [44][45][46][47] The PPA is to be signed within a 90-day window, financial closure is due 18 months from the effective date and scheduled commissioning is 24 months from the effective date. [48][49][50][51]

Eligibility: No prior project experience or commissioned capacity is required; the bidder need only deploy commercially established and operational solar PV, wind and ESS technologies. [52][53] Financially, the bidder must show net worth of INR 1.3 crore per MW, annual turnover of INR 63.8 lakh per MW and liquidity of INR 12.76 lakh per MW. [54][55][56][57] Consortia may bid and parent or affiliate credentials may be used, but controlling shareholding may not change from RfS submission until PPA execution, and the successful bidder (or consortium members combined) must hold at least 51% of the project company until one year after the SCSD. [58][59][60][61][62][63][64]

Money at risk: Bidders pay a bid processing fee of INR 3 lakh and furnish an Earnest Money Deposit of INR 9,28,000 per MW of solar, INR 12,64,000 per MW of wind and INR 14,64,000 per MW of ESS, subject to a maximum of Rs. 10 crore per project, valid for 12 months. [65][66][67][68][69][70][71] Before signing the PPA, selected bidders submit a Performance Bank Guarantee of INR 23,20,000 per MW of solar, INR 31,60,000 per MW of wind and INR 36,60,000 per MW of ESS, valid until 9 months after the Scheduled Commissioning Date, after which the EMD is returned. [72][73][74][75] An amount equal to the EMD is forfeited if the selected bidder fails to submit documents, meet eligibility or sign the PPA in time; the PBG is encashed per day in proportion to capacity not commissioned for delay beyond the SCSD, and is fully encashed with termination of the PPA for the un-commissioned capacity if delay exceeds SCSD plus 6 months. [76][77][78][79][80][81][82][83][84]

Tariff or payment: The successful bidder is paid a fixed tariff, bid in Rs/kWh and finalised through the e-reverse auction, under a PPA with a tenure of 25 years. [2][3][85][86][87][88][89][90][91][92][93] NHPC provides a monthly unconditional, revolving and irrevocable letter of credit sized at estimated average monthly billing, and the developer pays Payment Security Mechanism charges of 2 paisa per unit as a discount on monthly tariff payments. [94][95][96][97][98][99] Late payments carry a surcharge at SBI one-year MCLR plus 5% for the first month, rising 0.5% each further month and capped at 3% above the base rate, payable by NHPC subject to receipt from the Discom. [100][101][102]

Obligations and penalties: The developer must supply the contracted capacity with at least 90% availability during four daily peak hours (2 hours within 05:00-10:00 and 2 hours within 18:00-23:00, as scheduled by the Buying Entity), assessed monthly, and keep annual CUF within +10% / -15% of its declared value, with 100% of annual energy from RE. [12][13][14][15][103][16] Shortfall in peak-hour availability or in annual minimum energy is penalised at 1.5 times the tariff for the units not supplied, both may be levied in the same Contract Year, and continued failure is an Event of Default allowing termination and damages equal to 24 months of tariff for the contracted capacity. [104][105][106][107][108][109] Commissioning may be delayed up to 6 months beyond the SCSD with per-day encashment of the PBG, and delay beyond 6 months leads to termination; the developer also bears connectivity, land and all clearances and must use ALMM-listed equipment. [110][111][80][81][82][83][84][112][113][114][115][116][117][118][119][120]

NHPC also maintains a Payment Security Fund, for which the developer pays PSM charges of 2 paisa per unit (Rs. 0.02/kWh) as a discount on monthly tariff payments (RfS 3.13, PPA 10.4.9). scores.gold_value: Change in Law (PPA Art. 12.1.1) covers the enactment, amendment, modification or repeal of any Indian Law, a change in its interpretation or application by a Governmental Instrumentality or court, imposition of new consents/clearances/permits or new conditions for them, and any statutory change in tax structure or new tax applicable to setting up the project and supply of power after the bid submission date (bid date is the reference date for tax changes); it excludes changes in corporate income tax or withholding tax and regulatory measures by the Appropriate Commission. Relief (Art. 12.2) places the affected party (developer or Buying Entity) in the same financial position, with compensation determined under the Electricity (Timely Recovery of Costs due to Change in Law) Rules, 2021: 21 days' prior notice, computation furnished within 30 days, recovery through monthly tariff adjustment MT=(Y/X) as an annuity over a maximum of 180 months for non-recurring impacts (or until the impact persists for recurring ones), trued up annually, rounded to three decimals, and verified by the Appropriate Commission within sixty days.

scores.gold_value: On termination of the PPA for NHPC/Buying Entity default (after the consultation period and failed novation), NHPC/Buying Entities pay the developer damages equivalent to 24 months, or the balance PPA period if less, of charges for its contracted capacity at the stipulated minimum CUF/Availability, subject to NHPC receiving the amount from the Buying Entity/Discom; STU/CTU connectivity damages are borne by the Discom. If the PSA is terminated or reduced, any termination compensation paid by the Buying Entity is passed on to the developer after deducting NHPC's costs. For developer default by delay beyond SCSD + 6 months, a Generator Event of Default occurs, the PBG is encashed and the PPA for the un-commissioned capacity is terminated; no Termination Compensation is payable on termination for a Natural Force Majeure event beyond 180 days, only undisputed outstanding bills.

scores.gold_value: Under PPA Article 4.9, for grid unavailability beyond 175 hours in a year and for reduced offtake/backdown beyond 175 hours in a year, the buying entity/Discom pays Generation Compensation = (Tariff x RE power (MW) offered but not scheduled by Procurer) x 1000 x number of hours, at the PPA tariff (Article 9, excluding trading margin). The developer must sell the unscheduled power on the power exchange as price taker, and 95% of the amount realised after deducting expenses is adjusted against the compensation monthly; compensation is limited to the difference between actual generation up to declared/contracted capacity and the quantum scheduled, is paid with the energy bill of the month after receipt of REA, and carries no trading margin. The PSA (Art. 2.5) mirrors this and excludes compensation for backdown on grid security, safety or Force Majeure grounds.

scores.gold_value: Two shortfall rules apply, and both damages may be levied in the same Contract Year. (a) Shortfall in 90% availability of contracted capacity during Peak Hours, calculated monthly, for reasons attributable to the RPD/RE-PG: penalty applied to the shortfall in generation corresponding to the availability shortfall. (b) Failure in any Contract Year to supply minimum energy corresponding to the annual CUF within the permissible lower limit of the declared CUF (annual CUF to be maintained within (+)10% / (-)15% of declared value; illustration uses 85% of declared CUF). Penalty for both is equal to one and a half times the tariff for the number of units not supplied (illustrated in Annexure-1A / Schedule 4). Not applicable for Force Majeure or grid non-availability beyond the RPD's control, nor for the part Contract Year immediately after CSD. Continued failure to maintain minimum CUF / minimum availability is an Event of Default: the PPA is liable to be terminated and the RPD/RE-PG must pay damages equal to 24 months (or balance PPA period if less) of tariff for the contracted capacity, recoverable by forfeiture of the bank guarantee/POI.

scores.gold_value: (1) Failure of the selected bidder to submit the requisite documents, meet eligibility criteria or execute the PPA within the stipulated time: an amount equal to the EMD is encashed from the EMD or PBG as liquidated damages. (2) Delay in commencement of supply beyond SCSD (up to 6 months from SCSD/extended SCSD): the PBG/POI/Insurance Surety Bond is encashed on a per-day basis proportionate to the capacity not commissioned (e.g. PBG amount x (160/800) x (45/180), month = 30 days), applicable even where 0 MW is commissioned. (3) In addition to other remedies, the PBG/POI can be encashed to recover any damages/dues of the generator under the PPA; recovered amounts are credited to the Payment Security Fund. (4) On RPD/RE-PG Event of Default (failure to maintain minimum CUF/availability, assignment/novation contrary to PPA, repudiation, other uncured breaches), damages equal to 24 months of tariff may be recovered by forfeiture of the bank guarantee/POI. Failure to furnish and maintain the PBG is itself a material breach. PBG is returned after commissioning (within 45 days of SCSD under the PPA) after adjusting delay damages.

scores.gold_value: 'Firm and Dispatchable RE Power' means the power profile configuration defined in the RfS to be met by RE power sources: supply of contracted capacity from ISTS-connected RE projects (solar, wind or other MNRE-defined renewable) combined with ESS. The RPD must set up or tie up storage to meet the parameters for 'firmness and dispatchability', combining RE generation with energy storage (charged only from RE) to achieve the required peak-hour availability and annual CUF; the plant is made available to the buying utility and dispatched through its scheduling.

Not applicable for Force Majeure or grid non-availability, and not for the part Contract Year ending 31 March after CSD.
